name: Bhubaneswar
description: The Temple City of India, with hundreds of carved Kalinga-style temples, the Jain rock-cut caves of Udayagiri and Khandagiri, a lively Odia food scene and a large zoo and botanical park on the outskirts.

name: Puri
description: A sacred coastal town built around the Jagannath Temple, with a long golden beach, sunrise walks, fresh seafood, the Raghurajpur artists' village and easy day trips to Chilika Lake for birdwatching and dolphins.

name: Konark
description: Home to the UNESCO-listed 13th-century Sun Temple, carved as a giant stone chariot, with quiet beaches nearby and the annual Konark dance festival in December. Ideal for history and photography lovers.

name: Darjeeling
description: A misty Himalayan hill station famous for its tea gardens, sunrise views of Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill, the heritage toy train, colonial-era cafes and gentle trekking trails through peaceful forested ridges.

name: Gangtok
description: The clean, mountain-ringed capital of Sikkim with Buddhist monasteries, a pedestrian MG Marg, high-altitude glacial lakes like Tsomgo, scenic drives to Nathu La and views of the eastern Himalaya.

name: Manali
description: A mountain destination in the Kullu valley with trekking trails, snow at Solang and Rohtang, paragliding, river-side cafes in Old Manali, cedar forests, scenic landscapes and endless photography locations.

name: Shimla
description: The former British summer capital, with a car-free Ridge and Mall Road, colonial architecture, pine-forest walks, the Kalka–Shimla toy train and winter snow at nearby Kufri. Relaxed and family friendly.

name: Rishikesh
description: The yoga capital of the world on the Ganges, combining white-water rafting, riverside camping, bungee jumping and Himalayan foothill treks with evening aarti at Triveni Ghat and peaceful ashrams.

name: Goa
description: India's favourite beach destination with palm-lined sands, beach shacks, seafood, nightlife and flea markets in the north, quiet coves in the south, Portuguese-era churches and water sports along the coast.

name: Jaipur
description: The Pink City, with the hilltop Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal, City Palace and Jantar Mantar observatory, bustling bazaars for textiles and gems, and rich Rajasthani food. A cornerstone of the Golden Triangle.

name: Udaipur
description: The City of Lakes, known for sunset boat rides on Lake Pichola, the grand City Palace, rooftop restaurants, folk dance evenings at Bagore ki Haveli and a slow romantic pace ideal for couples.

name: Varanasi
description: One of the world's oldest living cities, with dawn boat rides along the ghats of the Ganges, the evening Ganga aarti, narrow lanes of temples and silk weavers, street food and nearby Sarnath.

name: Delhi
description: India's capital blends Mughal monuments like the Red Fort, Qutub Minar and Humayun's Tomb with world-class museums, the street food of Chandni Chowk, busy markets and a lively cafe and nightlife scene.

name: Mumbai
description: India's fast-paced financial capital, with the Gateway of India, sea-facing Marine Drive, the Elephanta Caves, colonial architecture, Bollywood, legendary street food, shopping and vibrant nightlife.

name: Bengaluru
description: The Garden City with a pleasant climate year-round, Lalbagh and Cubbon Park, a palace and museums, craft breweries, South Indian breakfast institutions and easy weekend drives to Nandi Hills.

name: Hyderabad
description: The City of Pearls, famous for Hyderabadi biryani, the Charminar and its bangle bazaars, the massive Golconda Fort, the Salar Jung Museum and Ramoji Film City.

name: Ooty
description: The Queen of the Nilgiris, with a UNESCO heritage mountain railway, botanical gardens, a boating lake, tea estates, eucalyptus forests and cool weather that makes it a classic family hill retreat.

name: Munnar
description: Rolling emerald tea plantations in the Western Ghats, misty viewpoints, waterfalls, trekking trails and the Eravikulam National Park, home of the endangered Nilgiri tahr. Peaceful and very photogenic.

name: Coorg
description: The Scotland of India, with coffee and spice plantations, misty hills, Abbey Falls, river camps, a Tibetan monastery at Bylakuppe and homestays serving Kodava cuisine. Great for nature and quiet trekking.

name: Srinagar
description: The summer capital of Kashmir, known for shikara rides and houseboats on Dal Lake, Mughal gardens, snow-capped mountain views and day trips to Gulmarg and Pahalgam for meadows, skiing and pony treks.

name: Leh
description: A high-altitude desert of stark mountains, Buddhist monasteries and turquoise lakes like Pangong, famed for road trips, motorbike adventures, high passes, trekking and dramatic landscape photography. Acclimatisation needed.

name: Port Blair
description: Gateway to the Andaman Islands, with the historic Cellular Jail and its light-and-sound show, Ross Island ruins, coral reefs for snorkelling at North Bay and ferry connections to the outer islands.

name: Havelock Island
description: A tropical island with Radhanagar, one of Asia's finest beaches, clear turquoise water, beginner-friendly scuba diving and snorkelling over coral reefs, beach sunsets and a slow relaxing island life.

name: Alleppey
description: The Venice of the East, where overnight houseboat cruises drift through palm-fringed backwater canals, paddy fields and villages, with Kerala seafood, quiet beaches and the famous snake-boat races in August.

name: Agra
description: Home of the Taj Mahal, the white marble symbol of love, alongside Agra Fort, the tomb of Itmad-ud-Daulah, sunset views from Mehtab Bagh and the abandoned Mughal city of Fatehpur Sikri nearby.

name: Amritsar
description: The spiritual heart of Sikhism around the shimmering Golden Temple and its free community kitchen, with the Jallianwala Bagh memorial, the Wagah border ceremony and some of India's best Punjabi food.

name: Jaisalmer
description: The Golden City in the Thar Desert, with a living sandstone fort, intricately carved havelis, camel safaris and desert camps on the Sam dunes, folk music under starry skies and the ghost village of Kuldhara.

name: Hampi
description: The vast boulder-strewn ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire, a UNESCO site of temples, royal enclosures and stone chariots, with coracle rides, sunset hill climbs, bouldering and a laid-back backpacker vibe.

name: Mysuru
description: A royal heritage city known for the illuminated Mysore Palace, the Dasara festival, Chamundi Hills, silk and sandalwood shopping, Brindavan Gardens and its famous soft dosas and Mysore pak.

name: Kolkata
description: The cultural capital of India, with colonial landmarks like the Victoria Memorial and Howrah Bridge, the Indian Museum, idol-makers of Kumartuli, Durga Puja, sweets, street food and a deep literary heritage.

name: Kochi
description: A historic port city where Chinese fishing nets line the shore of Fort Kochi, with Portuguese, Dutch and Jewish heritage, art cafes, the Mattancherry Palace, Kathakali performances and fresh Kerala seafood.

name: Pondicherry
description: A former French colony with mustard-yellow streets in White Town, a seaside promenade, French bakeries and cafes, the Sri Aurobindo Ashram, the experimental township of Auroville and quiet nearby beaches.

name: Ranthambore
description: One of the best places in India to see wild Bengal tigers on jeep and canter safaris, set around lakes and the ruins of a thousand-year-old fort inside the national park. A favourite of wildlife photographers.

name: Jim Corbett
description: India's oldest national park in the Himalayan foothills, with tiger and elephant safaris through sal forests and grasslands, river-side jungle lodges, birdwatching and nature walks along the Kosi river.

name: Kaziranga
description: A UNESCO-listed national park on the Brahmaputra floodplains, home to two-thirds of the world's one-horned rhinoceroses, plus wild elephants, tigers and water birds, explored by jeep safari and tea-garden walks.

name: Bodh Gaya
description: The place where the Buddha attained enlightenment, centred on the UNESCO-listed Mahabodhi Temple and the Bodhi tree, surrounded by monasteries built by Buddhist nations, meditation retreats and a calm spiritual atmosphere.
